name: Sazerac Martini
origin: Lands beyond Cador and the Eccentric East
appearance: A broad-shouldered gold dragonborn with a powerful, disciplined bearing. Sazerac's golden scales bear numerous small scars from his years of adventuring, and his attire is simple, practical, and meticulously maintained. He spends most of his waking hours at his forge and anvil, clad in a heavy leather smithing apron. His workshop is kept in immaculate order, with every tool and weapon afforded its proper place.
portrayal: Sazerac is composed, deliberate, and deeply devoted to honor. He speaks plainly but thoughtfully, rarely raising his voice or wasting words. He holds himself to exacting standards and respects those who demonstrate discipline, humility, and integrity, irrespective of their prowess in battle. Though ordinarily reserved, he takes considerable pleasure in discussing martial traditions, exceptional craftsmanship, and the proper use of a blade. His sense of humor is exceedingly dry and occasionally catches even his closest companions off guard.
motivations: Sazerac considers craftsmanship an extension of his martial philosophy: both demand patience, precision, and dedication. He takes pride in producing weapons worthy of those who wield them and regards the careless treatment of equipment as indicative of a broader lack of discipline. He is particularly interested in unfamiliar metallurgical traditions, ancient weapons, and techniques that have been lost to time. He willingly offers guidance to inexperienced warriors who demonstrate a sincere desire to improve themselves.
personal_circumstances: An accomplished warrior of the samurai tradition, Sazerac spent many years adventuring in distant lands, developing an appreciation for the relationship between a warrior and their equipment. His dedication to the martial arts eventually extended to the manufacture and maintenance of arms and armor. At the Wayward Spur, he has found a quieter means of practicing his discipline while equipping a new generation of adventurers.
relationships: Despite their shared prowess in battle, Sazerac and Flopthar Turdtoucher are near-perfect opposites in temperament. Their contrasting dispositions give rise to frequent banter, though each holds the other in considerable esteem. Sazerac respects Tabitha's ingenuity but remains skeptical of her more unconventional experiments, preferring proven techniques over needless complications. He treats Madame Zoria and her divinations with quiet reverence, though he believes that one's destiny is ultimately determined by one's actions.
knowledge_and_rumors: Sazerac maintains a modest selection of high-quality blades, melee weapons, and pieces of armor, which he sells to members of the Wayward League at their base prices. He repairs damaged arms and armor, accepts commissions for mundane equipment, and can assess the quality, craftsmanship, and potential origins of unfamiliar weapons. Although capable of working with unusual materials and producing exceptional equipment, more ambitious commissions, such as an entire suit of enchanted plate armor, may require the services of an outside specialist.
source_profile:
Sazerac Martini — Armorer
Lawful Good, male gold dragonborn, approaching middle age

Appearance. A broad-shouldered gold dragonborn with a powerful, disciplined bearing.
Sazerac's golden scales bear numerous small scars from his years of adventuring, and his attire
is simple, practical, and meticulously maintained. He spends most of his waking hours at his
forge and anvil, clad in a heavy leather smithing apron. His workshop is kept in immaculate
order, with every tool and weapon afforded its proper place.

Portrayal. Sazerac is composed, deliberate, and deeply devoted to honor. He speaks plainly
but thoughtfully, rarely raising his voice or wasting words. He holds himself to exacting
standards and respects those who demonstrate discipline, humility, and integrity, irrespective of
their prowess in battle. Though ordinarily reserved, he takes considerable pleasure in
discussing martial traditions, exceptional craftsmanship, and the proper use of a blade. His
sense of humor is exceedingly dry and occasionally catches even his closest companions off
guard.

Background. An accomplished warrior of the samurai tradition, Sazerac spent many years
adventuring in distant lands, developing an appreciation for the relationship between a warrior
and their equipment. His dedication to the martial arts eventually extended to the manufacture
and maintenance of arms and armor. At the Wayward Spur, he has found a quieter means of
practicing his discipline while equipping a new generation of adventurers.

Motivations. Sazerac considers craftsmanship an extension of his martial philosophy: both
demand patience, precision, and dedication. He takes pride in producing weapons worthy of
those who wield them and regards the careless treatment of equipment as indicative of a
broader lack of discipline. He is particularly interested in unfamiliar metallurgical traditions,
ancient weapons, and techniques that have been lost to time. He willingly offers guidance to
inexperienced warriors who demonstrate a sincere desire to improve themselves.

Relationships. Despite their shared prowess in battle, Sazerac and Flopthar Turdtoucher are
near-perfect opposites in temperament. Their contrasting dispositions give rise to frequent
banter, though each holds the other in considerable esteem. Sazerac respects Tabitha's
ingenuity but remains skeptical of her more unconventional experiments, preferring proven
techniques over needless complications. He treats Madame Zoria and her divinations with quiet
reverence, though he believes that one's destiny is ultimately determined by one's actions.

Services and Expertise. Sazerac maintains a modest selection of high-quality blades, melee
weapons, and pieces of armor, which he sells to members of the Wayward League at their base
prices. He repairs damaged arms and armor, accepts commissions for mundane equipment,
and can assess the quality, craftsmanship, and potential origins of unfamiliar weapons. Although
capable of working with unusual materials and producing exceptional equipment, more
ambitious commissions, such as an entire suit of enchanted plate armor, may require the
services of an outside specialist.

Adventure Hooks.

   ●​ The Mark of the Deep Forge. Sazerac recognizes a distinctive maker's mark on a piece
      of duergar metalwork brought to the Spur. Intrigued by its craftsmanship and troubled by
      its appearance among ordinary frontier goods, he asks the adventurers to investigate its
      provenance.
   ●​ A Worthy Blade. Sazerac learns of an unusual metal or forgotten smithing technique
      reputed to produce blades of exceptional quality. He commissions the adventurers to
      recover a sample of the material or a record of the technique, promising to put their
      discovery to good use at his forge.
source_reference: Handbook v0.4, pp. 16–17; newer staff entry supersedes Legendarium index
